title: Mother Jesus (Revelations 59–60)
hook: Julian speaks of our mother Christ, who feeds us with himself
tomorrow: after all those visions, what did Julian say they meant?

segments.voice: The lord and the servant: he fell rushing to serve, and the lord looked on him with pity and no blame. Julian finds another name for that kind of love.
screen: `HE FELL RUSHING TO SERVE.` → `ANOTHER NAME FOR THAT LOVE.`

segments.voice: A kid yells Mom from the other room before deciding what's even wrong. Some grown-ups still do it when they stub a toe. Julian of Norwich is choosing her words for Jesus. Lord, yes. Brother, yes. Then she writes one that can still catch a reader off guard: mother. Not Mary this time. Jesus. Our Mother Jesus, she writes, and she isn't being poetic for a line or two. She stays with it, and she explains herself.
screen: `A KID YELLS MOM.` → `LORD, BROTHER, AND...` → `OUR MOTHER JESUS.`

segments.voice: First, she doesn't trade one name for another. As truly as God is our Father, she says, so truly God is our Mother. Father stays. Mother is added. Then she works from what mothers actually do. A mother carries a child and brings it to birth; Julian says Jesus bears us into joy and endless life, and that this birth cost him the pain of the cross. A mother feeds her child; our precious Mother, Jesus, feeds us with himself, and she means the bread of communion. And a hurt or frightened child doesn't make a plan. It runs straight to its mother. That, Julian says, is how we're meant to run to him. She isn't far from the Gospels: in Matthew, Jesus says, "how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings." A neighbor tradition reaches for a mother too. In a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, sees a woman find her baby among a crowd of captives and hold it close to nurse it. God, he says, is more merciful to his servants than this woman is to her child. Two traditions, each looking at a mother to say something about God's love. The difference is honest: the hadith says God's mercy is greater than a mother's, without calling God a mother, and in Islam Jesus is honored as a prophet. Julian calls Jesus our mother.
screen: `TRULY FATHER, TRULY MOTHER.` · `HE BEARS US, AND FEEDS US.` · `A HEN GATHERING HER CHICKS.` · `A NEIGHBOR: MERCY BEYOND A MOTHER'S.` · then, large: `OUR PRECIOUS MOTHER.`

segments.voice: Do one small, mothering thing right now, for someone nearby or for yourself: fill a glass of water, set out tomorrow's lunch, plug in a phone that's dying. Do it slowly, the way a good parent does the tenth chore of the day, and then sit with whoever it was for in mind.
Mother Jesus. Julian's name for Christ, who carries us, feeds us with himself, and never stops loving us when we fall.
Keep this: our precious mother, the one a hurt child runs to without stopping to think. Good night, or good morning.

fork.setup: your little cousin asks at dinner: is God a boy or a girl? what could you say from Julian, true to her book?
options: God is only a Father, so a boy.
Julian keeps both: Father, and truly Mother.
fork.reveal: Julian writes that as truly as God is our Father, so truly God is our Mother. she adds a name; she doesn't trade one away.

trapdoor: what you thought: calling Jesus mother must be a new idea.
what it means: Julian builds it from what mothers do: carry, feed, gather a child that runs to them.
what a scholar hears: she keeps Father too, and Jesus' own image of a hen gathering her chicks is already in Matthew.
guess: Julian's name for Christ, who loves us as a mother does
a title Julian gave to Mary, the mother of Jesus
a nickname for the Church as every believer's mother
recall: a fall met with love, not blame

chat.says: pop says i'm 'mothering him to death.' i cut his food and fluffed his pillows. weird or sweet?
options: Sweet. Julian says Jesus loves like a mother: carrying, feeding, staying close.
Weird. Julian says mothering belongs to Mary alone, never to anyone else.
Weird. Julian called Jesus mother as a way of getting rid of Father.
chat.meaning: Julian builds her name for Jesus from what mothers do: carry, feed, and gather a hurt child close.

notes: Julian is paraphrased throughout (quoted: null), including 'as truly as God is our Father, so truly God is our Mother' (ch. 59) and 'our precious Mother, Jesus, feeds us with himself' (ch. 60); confirm against Warrack (1901) and quote if wanted.

The child running to its mother is drawn from ch. 61, just after the index's 59–60; confirm the chapter numbers in Warrack. The earlier draft's 'a mother lets a small child fall' line was cut for space.
The link between Julian's mother image and Matthew 23:37 is offered as the text's own neighbor ('she isn't far from the Gospels'), not as a claim about her sources.

Wisdom shape, unity thread: the neighbor is Islam. The hadith of the mother among the captives (Sahih al-Bukhari 5999; Sahih Muslim 2754) is paraphrased: the Prophet sees a woman find her child among the captives and nurse it, and says God is more merciful to his servants than she is to her child. Please have a Muslim reviewer confirm the numbering and wording, the honorific, and that the difference ('the hadith says God's mercy is greater than a mother's, without calling God a mother, and in Islam Jesus is honored as a prophet', leaning on Qur'an 19:30) is fair and unranked.
Glosses for hadith and Sahih al-Bukhari omit Arabic script because this path's lint allows only Greek or Latin script.
The fork answers a child's question ('is God a boy or a girl?') with a sentence a parent could say from Julian (the three-core-families note in RECIPE_V3).
